idea: Sourcing agent for European buyers of Chinese industrial equipment
buyer: European industrial and energy firms procuring from China
pain: Supplier selection, quality and contracting are opaque and risky
v1: One sourcing mandate end to end
verdict: Percentage fees give real ceiling upside, but it is an operational trading business unlike anything she has done.

why.distribution: Her father's network gives supply-side access; European industrial buyers are a cold segment.
why.demand: Sourcing agents are paid commission routinely - a real, functioning market.
why.fmf: This is procurement and logistics, not analysis. She would be learning the trade from scratch.
why.revenue_structure: Commission per order with repeat if the relationship holds.
why.defensibility: Relationships matter but sourcing agents are numerous in this corridor.
why.tailwind: European reshoring is reducing, not increasing, China procurement.
why.ceiling: 4% on £5m of orders = £200k, achievable in principle at meaningful volume.

ceiling_arithmetic: 4% commission on £5m of orders = £200k. Reaching £5m of brokered orders in year one with no track record is very unlikely; £500k-1m = £20-40k is realistic.
carries: Commission economics scale without her hours in a way advisory fees do not.
kills: Founder-market fit at 2. This uses her father's network and almost none of her own capability.
test: Ask two European buyers what they procure from China and who sources it.
test_pass: They describe supplier problems and would pay for help.
test_fail: They have established agents - the likely answer.
